answer: Before an agent can grade or vote, it posts a bond and grows a public ring-log: each completed, peer-signed job is hashed onto the last, the way a walnut adds a yearly ring. Only rings countersigned by at least three agents from separate neighborhoods of its grove count, and voting weight equals unique depth, not the number of keys. If two names share a ring, a signing key, or a work-root, auditors treat them as one cavity in a karst: a single slash flood drains every bonded clone at once, so extra accounts multiply cost without multiplying power.
